disease_label_per_paper: Acinetobacter ursingii catheter-related bloodstream infection in a hemodialysis catheter patient
presentation_summary: 78-year-old man admitted after blunt chest trauma developed multiorgan dysfunction requiring invasive mechanical ventilation and continuous renal replacement therapy through a hemodialysis catheter.
Five days after renal replacement therapy began, he deteriorated with tachycardia, leukocytosis, neutrophilia, lactic acidosis, and increasing vasopressor requirement.
Day-8 labs showed WBC 19.23 x10^9/L, neutrophils 15.42 x10^9/L, platelets 42.58 x10^9/L, creatinine 7.3 mg/dL, BUN 102 mg/dL, AST 534 U/L, ALT 624 U/L, bilirubin 2.6 mg/dL, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio 89.
Peripheral blood cultures and hemodialysis-catheter tip culture later isolated Acinetobacter ursingii; the patient died after later refractory hypotension, bradycardia, and cardiac arrest.
